title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
title_zh: 文献研究：Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
summary: The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations,…
abstract: The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. By tracking the loss distribution via an exponential moving average, this unsupervised method identifies outliers throughout a single training run. We show that this approach prevents overfitting and matches the performance of iterative refinement baselines with significantly reduced overhead. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated by recovering accurate physical observables for liquid water from unconverged reference data, including diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, we validate its scalability by training a foundation model for organic chemistry on the SPICE dataset, where it reduces both energy and force errors. This framework provides a simple, automated solution for training robust models on imperfect datasets across dataset sizes.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

The data reveal large nonsaturating magnetoresistance and a Hall response strongly nonlinear in magnetic field, arising from multiple electron- and hole-like carriers with mobilities approaching 3000 cm 2 /Vs. Mobility-spectrum analysis shows that higher fields resolve additional carrier populations hidden at lower fields. Thermal transport exhibits a similarly nonlinear field dependence and deviations from the Wiedemann–Franz law, indicating additional phononic or magnonic heat-conduction channels. [Phys. Rev. title: Gyrotropy from extrinsic geometry in twisted materials
title_zh: 文献研究：Gyrotropy from extrinsic geometry in twisted materials
summary: Author(s): Spenser Talkington and Eugene J. Mele Two-dimensional moiré materials feature widely tunable electronic structures. When these materials are illuminated by light, they exhibit optical gyrot…
abstract: Author(s): Spenser Talkington and Eugene J. Mele Two-dimensional moiré materials feature widely tunable electronic structures. When these materials are illuminated by light, they exhibit optical gyrotropy in the form of circular dichroism and birefringence. Here, the authors show that this gyrotropy naturally decomposes into an intrinsic contribution due to interlayer electronic coupling and an extrinsic contribution due to the twisted embedding of the material in physical space. The authors conduct a general symmetry analysis applicable to moiré materials and identify regimes in which the intrinsic, and in which the extrinsic contributions dominate the gyrotropy. Finally, they apply the analysis to twisted bilayer graphene and twisted MoTe 2 . [Phys. Rev. B 114, 235408] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026

title: Building new non-empirical hybrid and double-hybrid density functionals from the TCA family of GGA expressions
title_zh: 文献研究：Building new non-empirical hybrid and double-hybrid density functionals from the TCA family of GGA expressions
summary: The Tognetti–Cortona–Adamo (TCA) correlation functional, and their subsequent variants, constitutes an important family of nonempirical generalized gradient approximations that have found successful a…
abstract: The Tognetti–Cortona–Adamo (TCA) correlation functional, and their subsequent variants, constitutes an important family of nonempirical generalized gradient approximations that have found successful applications in molecular and solid-state electronic structure calculations. In this work, we present a systematic assessment of the original TCA functional together with the revTCA, gracTCA, and transTCA variants within nonempirical hybrid (TCA0) and double-hybrid (TCA-QIDH) frameworks. Their performance is evaluated using the comprehensive GMTKN55 benchmark database, including more detailed analysis of the challenging MB16-43 and SIE4x4 subsets, as well as three different global performance metrics: WTMAD-2A, WTMAD-2B, and the recently proposed WTMAD-4. The results reveal a consistent improvement in accuracy upon ascending “Jacob’s ladder,” with the nonempirical double-hybrid models reducing the global errors by approximately a factor of 2–3 relative to their GGA counterparts. Among the semilocal functionals, the original TCA correlation provides the most balanced overall performance, while the differences among the various TCA-based models become much less pronounced at the double-hybrid level. Importantly, the relative ranking of the functionals is essentially unaffected by the choice of the WTMAD metric, demonstrating the robustness of the conclusions with respect to the weighting scheme adopted for the GMTKN55 database. The remaining deficiencies are associated with dispersion-dominated intermolecular interactions, highlighting the potential use of some long-range correlation corrections. Overall, this study confirms that the TCA functional, particularly when adopted in a double-hybrid scheme, constitutes a reliable and transferable framework for the development of accurate density functional approximations applicable to a broad range of chemical problems.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

title: Cooling down trees for finite-temperature quantum dynamics: Purification within ML-MCTDH
title_zh: 文献研究：Cooling down trees for finite-temperature quantum dynamics: Purification within ML-MCTDH
summary: Simulating multidimensional quantum systems at finite temperature is inherently challenging as the system is no longer described by a single, pure-state wavefunction but by a density operator, squarin…
abstract: Simulating multidimensional quantum systems at finite temperature is inherently challenging as the system is no longer described by a single, pure-state wavefunction but by a density operator, squaring an already exponential scaling of the Hilbert space. Building upon the compact wavefunction ansatz of the multi-layer multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree (ML-MCTDH) method, we present a new scheme for simulating finite-temperature quantum dynamics based on purification. Here, a density operator is mapped to a single ML-MCTDH wavefunction in an enlarged Hilbert space, comprising physical and auxiliary degrees of freedom. In the key step, one obtains a pure-state representation of the canonical density operator via imaginary time-propagation of the infinite-temperature state. The most important observation is that this state can be exactly decomposed as a Hartree product of maximally entangled combined modes, each combined mode consisting of a physical degree of freedom and its auxiliary counterpart. Through dynamically pruning the node ranks of the ML-tree during the “cool down” stage yields a compact finite-temperature wavefunction, thus accelerating the real-time propagation and enabling finite-temperature simulations of multidimensional, correlated molecular systems. Our method circumvents both intensive statistical sampling and costly tensor-decomposition of the full density-operator, while being broadly applicable to model Hamiltonians and general ab initio potential energy surfaces alike. Two applications of the method are presented: benchmark results on the thermal ground-state of H 2 O, as well as temperature-dependent infrared absorption spectra of the more challenging, floppy H3O2− anion.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

title: Correlating Charge-Storage Kinetics, Quantum Capacitance, and Surface Charge Density in Bi2O2S: An Experimental-DFT Study
title_zh: Bi2O2S 中电荷存储动力学、量子电容和表面电荷密度的关联：实验 DFT 研究
summary: 了解层状电极材料中的电荷存储需要将电化学动力学与电极积累电子电荷的固有能力区分开来。在这里，使用电化学测量和密度泛函理论 (DFT) 计算研究了相纯 Bi2O2S，以建立这种关系。循环伏安法、恒电流充放电和电化学阻抗谱揭示了强烈的速率依赖性电荷存储响应，在 1 A g-1 时比电容为 866 F g-1。扫描速率依赖性给出的平均 b 值为 ~ 0.61，而 Dunn 分析表明，扩散依赖性过程主导着电荷存储响应。
abstract: Understanding charge storage in layered electrode materials requires distinguishing electrochemical kinetics from the intrinsic ability of the electrode to accumulate electronic charge. Here, phase-pure Bi2O2S was investigated using electrochemical measurements and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to establish this relationship. Cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge-discharge, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed a strongly rate-dependent charge-storage response, with a specific capacitance of 866 F g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹. The scan-rate dependence gave an average b-value of ~ 0.61, while Dunn analysis showed that diffusion-dependent processes dominate the charge-storage response. DFT calculations further demonstrated that surface modification alters the electronic charge-storage ability of Bi2O2S. The calculated quantum capacitance increased from 493.14 (:μ:Fcm⁻²) for the pristine surface to 638.75 (:μ:Fcm⁻²) following OH adsorption. Surface charge densities of 513.46 and 506.76 (:μ:C:cm⁻²) were obtained for K-top and K-hollow configurations, respectively. Experimental surface charge densities approached the DFT-derived range at higher current densities, whereas larger deviations at lower current densities indicate additional contributions from electrolyte-mediated and Faradaic processes. These results establish an experimental-DFT framework for relating rate-dependent electrochemical charge storage to the intrinsic electronic charge-accumulation behaviour of Bi2O2S.

title: From nonmagnetic to magnetic: A 2D semiconductor with electrically tunable magnetism
title_zh: 从非磁性到磁性：一种具有电可调磁性的2D半导体
summary: 新加坡国立大学（ NUS ）的研究人员与瑞士、捷克共和国和德国机构的科学家合作，展示了一种将磁性引入非磁性二维（ 2D ）半导体的方法，随后使用电压控制其磁性。该研究结果发表在《科学进展》杂志上，为研究原子薄材料中的电可控磁性建立了一个新的平台，对未来的自旋电子技术具有潜在的影响。
abstract: Researchers from the National University of Singapore (NUS), in collaboration with scientists from institutions in Switzerland, the Czech Republic and Germany, have demonstrated a way to introduce magnetism into an otherwise nonmagnetic two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor and subsequently control its magnetic properties using an electrical voltage. The findings, published in Science Advances, establish a new platform for investigating electrically controllable magnetism in atomically thin materials, with potential implications for future spintronic technologies.
